offers.title: The freshen-up
offers.text: A bath and brush for a coat that needs a reset.

offers.title: The full groom
offers.text: A complete visit with a haircut shaped around coat and lifestyle.

offers.title: The gentle introduction
offers.text: A conversation and a shorter introduction for a first visit.

story.title: Every dog brings a different story.
story.text: Tell your groomer what your dog likes, what worries them, and what has worked before. A good visit begins with a conversation, not an assumption.

guide.title: Help us get to know your best friend.
guide.intro: A little preparation helps a real groomer understand the dog behind the appointment.

notes.title: Tell the whole story
notes.text: Share coat history, previous grooming experiences, sensitivities, and any concerns. Health questions belong with your veterinarian.

notes.title: Talk about the coat
notes.text: Matting, tangles, and shedding affect the plan. A groomer should explain comfortable options and avoid promising a style before assessing the coat.

notes.title: Prepare for arrival
notes.text: Confirm the business’s vaccination, leash, pickup, and late-arrival policies directly. This fictional example does not invent medical or vaccination requirements.

notes.title: Plan the next visit
notes.text: Coat type, home maintenance, and lifestyle help determine a useful grooming rhythm. Ask for a routine that fits your dog rather than a universal schedule.

faq.a: A real groomer should discuss behavior and handling needs first. The planner includes a comfort question to start that conversation.

faq.q: Can I choose a haircut from a photo?
faq.a: A reference can help, but coat type, condition, and comfort influence the result. The style is confirmed with the groomer.
No. This is a grooming example. Medical concerns should be discussed with a qualified veterinarian.
